title: Mind the Feed: Scrolling Behavior, Online Content, and Well-Being
summary: This project investigates social media scrolling behavior and its relationship to well-being in a healthy population. It aims to develop and validate a new naturalistic experimental scrolling task that captures key features of everyday social media use while enabling controlled measurement of behavior and subjective experience. The task will be made applicable to be presented in an functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) setting. In addition, a new questionnaire will be developed to assess perceived individual online content environments, including emotional tone, thematic structure, and perceived algorithmic personalization. Using a cross-cultural design with data collected in Germany and Korea, the study examines how different forms of scrolling, such as affect-driven engagement with negative content and passive habitual scrolling, are associated with stress and well-being. The project provides methodological foundations for future research on the cognitive, affective, and neural mechanisms of social media engagement.
conditions: Only healthy participants are included in this study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Fluency in German/Korean, normal or corrected-to-normal vision and report regular use of social media feeds in everyday life (minimum 1h per week).
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are a history of neurological disorders, current or past severe psychiatric disorders, and the use of medication that substantially affects central nervous system functioning.
